title: AI Maestro Project Plan
description: Canonical schema for board/plan.json — the project plan every epic and ticket is scoped against. Items carry stable ids (D-/UC-/FR-/NFR-/M-/OUT-) so a ticket's `traces_to` can point at one and the scope gate can check it. board/plan.md is a generated mirror of this file and is never the source of truth.

planVersion.description: Schema generation of this file. 1 today; bumped only by a migrating release.

sections.description: One key per plan section. A section absent, empty, or holding only placeholder text counts as unfilled toward the completeness percentage.

goal.description: What success means for the whole project — not a feature list.

text.description: One or two sentences: the outcome the project exists to produce.

metrics.description: Measurable signals that the goal was met.

scope.description: The boundary the scope gate enforces. `out` entries carry ids so a ticket can be caught tracing to work the plan deliberately excluded.

in.description: Free-text statements of what is in scope. Narrative only — the enforceable in-scope surface is the ids in deliverables/useCases/functional/nonFunctional/milestones.

text.description: Something this project deliberately will not do. A ticket tracing to this id is a scope violation.

actor.description: Who performs it. Blank is allowed but weakens the use case.

text.description: What the actor does, and why it matters to them.
One behaviour the system must have. One requirement per entry — an entry with 'and' in it is usually two.

verify.description: How it is demonstrated: a test command, a manual check, a metric. The release gate reads this.

text.description: The quality attribute: performance, security, availability, accessibility, compliance, operability.

budget.description: The measurable bar — 'p95 < 300ms', 'WCAG 2.2 AA', '99.9% monthly'. An NFR with no budget cannot be gated.

verify.description: How the budget is measured. The release gate requires evidence against this for any ticket tracing here.

target.description: Optional date or condition. Free text — the kit never schedules from it.

gap.description: Something a reporting skill (atomic-report, repo-audit, scale, data-model, orchestration-health) found the plan does not cover. Open REQUIRED gaps count against the completeness percentage; optional ones are suggestions and never do.

text.description: The gap, stated as what the plan is missing — not as a fix.

need.description: required = the plan is incomplete without it; optional = worth considering.

from.description: The skill or person that raised it, e.g. "atomic-report".

status.description: open = unaddressed; accepted = folded into the plan (record the id it became in `resolvedAs`); declined = deliberately not doing it. Only `open` affects completeness.

resolvedAs.description: The plan item id this gap became when accepted, e.g. "FR-7".
